The problem today

Every new product reaches manufacturing with the same unanswered question.

The design is released. Now someone has to work out whether it can actually be built. The answer is spread across CAD, PLM, ERP, supplier portals, spreadsheets and email, and it is pieced together by hand, usually late.

01 · MANUAL BOM

BOMs are rebuilt by hand

Quantities, part numbers and attributes are retyped from CAD into spreadsheets. Gaps stay hidden until someone downstream needs the field.

02 · DUPLICATES

New part numbers for parts you already own

Nobody can search the catalogue by function, so the same connector is created again. Each duplicate adds qualification, inventory and supplier cost.

03 · LATE SURPRISES

Readiness problems show up at release

Blank ERP fields, a revision mismatch or a supplier who cannot deliver in time are found when the build is already committed.

04 · NO OWNERSHIP

Nobody knows who fixes what

Issues sit in email threads and status meetings. There is no single view of what blocks the build, how much it matters and who must act.

Can we build 5,000 units of this module at the Bengaluru plant within 60 days? Today this takes days of cross-checking across teams. The Studio answers it in seconds, shows why and tells you what to do next.
The solution

One flow, three questions, from the CAD file to a build decision.

Each step answers a question the business already asks. The results carry forward, so by Step 3 the decision rests on clean data and parts you have already rationalised.

1CAD to BOM

What is in this product?

Load a STEP file and get a bill of materials you can trust.

  • The structure, quantities and properties come straight from the CAD model, with the source of every value recorded.
  • Click any part, in 3D or in the tree, to see its cost, suppliers, stock, alternates and lifecycle.
  • Missing data is listed with a suggested value. Engineers fix it directly or through a change order.
10part types, 24 parts in the demo module
70%metadata complete on arrival
39gaps found, each with a fix
2Rationalization

Do we already own these parts?

Every new part is compared with the approved catalogue before it gets a number.

  • Parts are matched on specifications, form, fit and function, not just on names.
  • Each part gets a clear verdict: identical to an existing part, similar, or genuinely new.
  • Sourcing questions are answered in place: who supplies it, at what price and with what lead time.
5parts already exist, reuse them
2similar, engineer reviews
3genuinely new parts
3Production readiness

Can we build it, here, in time?

Ask for a quantity, a plant and a date. Get a decision you can defend.

  • Every part is checked against four gates: ERP handover, configuration, revision and sourcing.
  • Each blocker says what is wrong, why it matters, how to fix it and who owns it.
  • Fixes are applied through an approved ECO, and the score updates straight away.

Dashboards

Four dashboards, each answering a question a different team asks.

Every dashboard has the copilot built in. Point at any chart or table, ask about it and download the report.

How it fits your landscape

It sits on top of the systems you already run and replaces none of them.

The Studio reads from your CAD, PLM, ERP and supply data, works out the answers and hands each decision to the right team. Changes go back only through governed change orders.

Numbers you can trace

Every score and shortage is calculated by rules you can inspect. The AI explains results and never makes up a figure.

No silent changes

The copilot can read freely but change nothing on its own. Every fix becomes a change order with a named approver.

Runs in your network

Deployed on your servers next to your data. Only the answer to a question is sent to the AI service, and it also works with no AI at all.

Built to scale

Each question reads only the rows for that product, so answers stay fast as your databases grow to millions of records.

Business value

Fewer new part numbers, earlier warnings, faster decisions.

These figures come from the demo product and its sample data. In a pilot we measure the same things on your products.

50%

Of new parts already existed

5 of the 10 parts in the power module matched an approved part exactly. Reusing them avoids five new part numbers and their qualification, stock and supplier overhead.

Where we are

Built and working today. Ready for a pilot on your data.

Done so far

  • CAD to BOM from STEP AP203, AP214 and AP242, plus drawings and BOM spreadsheets, with an interactive 3D viewer
  • Part intelligence: cost, suppliers, stock, alternates and metadata for every part
  • Data completeness scoring, with fixes made directly or through change orders
  • Rationalization: identical, similar or new for every part, plus sourcing answers
  • Production readiness: four gates, blockers with owners, what-if on quantity, plant and date
  • Governed fixes: ECO workflow with approval roles and an audit trail
  • Four dashboards, each with “ask about an area” and report download
  • Copilot working through 51 approved tools, which also runs without AI
  • Works on files or PostgreSQL with identical results
